html:
The Jaminjung are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, in country along the lower Victoria River, near the border with Western Australia.

Their language is closely related to that of the Ngaliwurru, and the two peoples share much of their culture. Other neighbours are the Murrinh-Patha to the north and the Miriwoong to the west. From the 1880s cattle stations took over the Victoria River district, and Jaminjung people worked on them for generations. The language is still spoken by some today. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
